title: Filtered-colimit hull closure for an essentially small FP2 weak Serre subcategory
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a locally small Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with all small colimits in the indexing universe. Let $\mathcal C\subset\mathcal B$ be an essentially small full replete subcategory containing zero and closed under ambient kernels, cokernels, and extensions. Suppose that for every $C\in\mathcal C$ and every small filtered diagram $(B_i)$ in $\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the natural maps $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}(C,B_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}(C,\varinjlim_i B_i)$ and $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathrm{Yon}}(C,B_i)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathrm{Yon}}(C,\varinjlim_i B_i)$ are bijective. Yoneda $\operatorname{Ext}^1(C,B)$ means equivalence classes of ambient short exact sequences $0\to B\to M\to C\to0$, with Baer sum. In this Grothendieck setting, render these Yoneda groups by the small degree-one Ext groups of [def-pc-ext] through the canonical natural Baer-group comparison, which identifies pushout of extensions with covariant functoriality in the second variable. Thus the displayed Yoneda continuity condition is equivalently preservation of small filtered colimits by $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal B}(C,-)$ in that model; no comparison or finite-stage lift is an additional hypothesis. Let $\mathcal J$ be the full replete class of small filtered colimits in $\mathcal B$ of objects of $\mathcal C$, with arbitrary morphisms in the diagrams. Then $\mathcal J$ contains zero and $\mathcal C$, is closed under all small filtered ambient colimits and all small ambient coproducts, and is closed under ambient kernels, cokernels and extensions. In the extension assertion every ambient short exact sequence is included, without any assumed lift to finite stages. All resulting presentations use small indexing categories in the same universe.

proof.text: A constant singleton presentation gives P ≤ ind(P), and therefore zero lies in ind(P). Hom continuity identifies P-objects as finitely presentable. Apply ObjectProperty.ind_ind to flatten a filtered colimit of filtered P-presentations. This proves the small filtered-colimit closure used throughout the remaining proof.

Given a filtered P-presentation p of X, prove its functor to CostructuredArrow P.ι X is final: every map out of a P-object factors through a stage by finite presentability, and two maps to one stage that agree in X agree after a transition. For f:X→Y and chosen presentations pX,pY, take the comma category of pX.toCostructuredArrow followed by postcomposition with f, and pY.toCostructuredArrow. Since the latter functor is final and both indices are filtered, the comma category is filtered and both projections are final (Mathlib Comma.Final). Its diagram consists of the stage arrows, and its cocone to f is colimiting because both endpoint cocones are colimiting (Comma.fstSndJointlyReflectColimit). Its object type is small as a sigma of two small indices and small Hom sets; its homs are small as pairs of index morphisms. Reindex via SmallModel to obtain a presentation in the same universe. No finite colimits or skeleton of P are needed for this step.

Apply arrow_exact_colimits to the filtered arrow presentation. Grothendieck exactness gives its hypothesis. Mapping the presentation through ker and coker presents the ambient kernel and cokernel by kernels and cokernels of stage arrows, which belong to P. Transport across the unique kernel/cokernel isomorphisms to get closure for every kernel fork and cokernel cofork, as required by the ObjectProperty classes.

Present X⊞Y using the product of chosen filtered presentations: the stage is the binary biproduct of the two stage objects, which belongs to P by extension closure. Each coordinate projection is final. A cocone on the stage biproducts is exactly a pair of cocones on the coordinate diagrams, by the two biproduct inclusions. Their colimit universal properties therefore give the colimit X⊞Y. Zero and binary coproducts imply finite coproduct closure by Mathlib ObjectProperty.FiniteProducts. In particular, a pushout of hull objects is again a hull object: in an abelian category it is the cokernel of (u,-a) into the binary biproduct, and step 3 applies.

For a short exact sequence 0→N→M→C→0 with N in ind(P) and C in P, map a chosen filtered P-presentation of N through extFunctorObj C 1 and then forget to types. Ext continuity and elementwise surjectivity give a stage D_i and an Ext-one class ξ over D_i mapping to the class of the original sequence. The existing degree-one extension classification theorem represents ξ by 0→D_i→E→C→0. Extension closure gives P(E). Push this sequence out along D_i→N using pushout_short_exact_sequence. Naturality of extClass identifies the class of this pushout with the original class. The injectivity clause of the classification theorem supplies an endpoint-fixed isomorphism of middle objects. The pushout is in the hull by step 4, so M is too. This avoids constructing the filtered undercategory of a chosen kernel stage.

For an arbitrary short exact sequence with both endpoints in the hull, present its quotient as a filtered colimit of P-objects and pull the sequence back to each stage. ShortComplex.ShortExact.pullback, the dual pushout assertion, gives short exactness with unchanged kernel. Step 5 puts all these middle terms in the hull. Mathlib IsColimit.pullbackOfHasExactColimitsOfShape computes their colimit as the original middle term, using that the filtered index is connected and that Grothendieck filtered colimits are exact. The pullbackObjIso comparison and pullbackSymmetry identify its pointwise pullbacks with ShortComplex.pullback. Step 1 finishes extension closure.

Finally, the ambient coproduct of any small family is the filtered colimit of its finite subsums, using Mathlib CoproductsFromFiniteFiltered.liftToFinsetColimitCocone. The stages lie in the hull by step 4 (or extension closure), and step 1 puts their colimit in the hull. Finset(Discrete I) is small in the same universe and filtered, including for empty I.

proof_origin.place: F4 stage-3 proof, 2026-10-24. tool_uses.why: Generic finality and undercategory facts, applied dually to small filtered categories. The compactification-coherence unit has no category-theoretic substitute.
Ambient abelian pushout theorem, also applied in the opposite category to form pullback extensions. It is a generic tool, not a replacement of a geometric unit step.
Generic preservation of kernel/cokernel cocones by exact colimits; needed for arrow presentations and the final pullback colimit, independently of the geometric ind-heart hypotheses.
